newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Leftist leader warns Rome on welfare cuts.
newsitem.headline: Leftist leader warns Rome on welfare cuts.

text.p: Italian hard-left leader Fausto Bertinotti, whose party holds the balance of power in Rome, warned the centre-left government on Saturday against trying to cut welfare benefits in its battle to find budget savings.

Bertinotti, whose small Communist Refoundation gives Prime Minister Romano Prodi his majority in the lower Chamber of Deputies, said that his party would oppose any attempt to reduce spending on health and pensions.
"I hope Prodi stays on for a long time...but for that he must think of (a package of) social reform that does not cut pensions or the health sector," he told journalists in Lisbon.
Bertinotti, who was in the Portuguese capital for a rally of European far-left parties, said that his party would vote in parliament against any policies of which it did not approve.
"That is obvious," said Bertinotti, whose party nearly toppled Prodi in April when it refused to back the sending of a security force to Albania.

The government is expected to present next week plans to slash some 25 trillion lire ($15 billion) off the 1998 budget deficit in an effort to convince its sceptical European Union partners that Italy can make the grade for a planned single currency in 1999.
The single currency stipulates a series of economic entry targets, few of which Italy, a founder member of the European bloc, currently meets.
Italian newspapers have reported that around a third of the savings will come from welfare cuts, although Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi denied on Friday that any decisions had been taken.
Bertinotti said that his party wanted reform of the welfare system to make it more efficicient, not to reduce it.
"This government cannot pursue a policy of cuts in social spending," he said.
